title: The Alpha Was Always for Sale

Truth Social is selling a head start. Pay enough and you get Trump's posts before the rest of the market does — the same posts that this year alone have moved oil, semiconductors, and the dollar depending on what mood tariffs were in that morning. Nobody's calling it insider trading, since nothing is technically inside. The information reaches everyone else seconds later, just delayed and priced accordingly.

What gets me is the incentive sitting underneath it. A platform that profits from selling early access to volatile posts has a straightforward reason to keep the posts volatile. Not a conspiracy, just alignment: Truth Social wants engagement and paying subscribers, and market-moving tariff bombs are the highest-engagement content the President produces. The product isn't the post anymore, it's the seconds between the post and everyone else finding out.

A few floors over at Treasury, Bessent's running the opposite trade this week. Quiet, old-school yen intervention, reportedly $5 to $10 billion, leaked to Reuters via a photographed to-do list (its own small comedy), aimed at smoothing out a currency move nobody wanted to see accelerate. One arm of the same administration is spending real money to dampen a market surprise, while a company one arm's-length away sells market surprise by the minute.

I don't think anyone planned that contrast on purpose. That's what makes it worth sitting with: a government that treats volatility as a fire to put out and as a subscription tier, in the same week, and both instincts probably feel sincere from the inside. Markets have always priced information asymmetry. It's rarer to see someone hand you the menu.
